title: A nocturne between keys and strings
work: Nocturne in E♭ major, Op. 9 No. 2
question: What changes when Elman’s violin sustains the melody that Lévy and Prati play on piano?
intro: Lévy’s Musopen performance is dated circa 2014; Prati’s live account comes from Madrid on 24 November 2015. Elman plays a violin-and-piano transcription, but Victor 74052 covers several masters: his date, take and pianist remain unresolved. The provisional piano map covers Lévy 0–260 and Prati 0–290 seconds. Elman is mapped only in the opening, Lévy 0–65 to Elman 3–82; a full-piece trial failed to follow later recurring material. His pitch features are shifted one semitone for analysis, not playback. Even in this opening, lower confidence requires caution: the map is a listening aid, not evidence of exact bar identity or instrument technique.

passages.label: Melody and accompaniment
passages.note: Compare a bowed melodic line with a pianist’s decaying notes; the maps locate passages, not individual articulations.

passages.label: Within the opening phrase
passages.note: Compare the space around the line’s smaller attacks. Elman’s opening map is provisional, not a note-for-note alignment.

passages.label: After the first rise
passages.note: Lévy settles after the preceding rise. Compare how the other performers make room before continuing; Elman’s coverage ends at reference second 65.

passages.label: The ornamented line
passages.note: Lévy and Prati only: follow the whole phrase through its smaller attacks. Elman has no published correspondence here.

passages.label: Later expansion
passages.note: Lévy and Prati only: compare the rise and retreat without turning recording level into a claim about loudness.

passages.label: Closing build
passages.note: Lévy and Prati only: compare the broad ascent with its ornamental release.

passages.label: Last cadential sound
passages.note: Lévy and Prati only: listen beyond arrival into resonance. Their map intentionally excludes the final low-level tails.
